title: new02; found by us, still unfixed
live_proof: verified in the pin on 2026-10-16, by reading all three sites and by measurement. jsonEachColumn's default arm (the ROOT column) does 'const char *zRoot = p->zRoot; if( zRoot==0 ) zRoot = "$"; sqlite3_result_text(ctx, zRoot, -1, SQLITE_STATIC)', so the cursor's own buffer is handed to the SQL layer with no copy; jsonEachFilter allocates it with sqlite3_malloc64 and memcpy; jsonEachCursorReset frees it. Host ASan: heap-use-after-free, 0 bytes inside a freed 8-byte region, read by memcmp under binCollFunc (sqlite3.c:144244) <- vdbeCompareMemString <- sqlite3MemCompare <- minmaxStep, freed by sqlite3_free <- jsonEachCursorReset (sqlite3.c:185490) <- jsonEachFilter. WHAT CANNOT BE CHECKED FROM HERE: the 'unfixed' label. That the defect is live in 3.22.0 is verified above; that upstream has still not fixed this sibling arm is the lane's reading of 28001204f4 and cannot be confirmed offline. The corpus measures the pin, so the label affects provenance rather than any verdict
object: p->zRoot, the cursor's own malloc'd copy of the path argument, handed out as SQLITE_STATIC
lifetime_ender: re-filtering the cursor per outer row calls jsonEachCursorReset, which frees the previous zRoot while an accumulator still holds the pointer
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator. Found by us rather than collected: it is the sibling arm the upstream fix left behind, which is why upstream_fix is 'unfixed' and not a commit. Same shape and same consumer as case 14 -- the earlier text said case 18 (withdrawn, campaign numbering), which is the unrelated memsys5 demonstrator; the reference was to 17. The two are kept apart on the object, not the instruction: 17 hands out p->zJson from the JEACH_JSON arm, which upstream converted to SQLITE_TRANSIENT, and this one hands out p->zRoot from the default arm, which it did not. Upstream fixing one arm and not the other is itself the argument that they are separable

status: re-measured 2026-10-16 on this platform: host ASan reports the use-after-free; virtual-malloc MISSED with both controls as declared (cross_rows=6, rows=1, RETURNED); virtual-nested-pools CAUGHT, cause=25 pc=0x3fae630198 in memcmp attributed by function and corroborated by probe site 52's pointer identity, both controls as declared; cheribsd-revocation MISSED, cross_rows=6, rows=1, RETURNED rc=0, with the boot's positive control trapping. Both of the case's own reachability probes held in every run: the cross join produces 6 rows and the root column is '$.bb', so the malloc'd-path branch was taken rather than the literal fallback. The arms block below is the 2026-10-11 bundle's and is regenerated by derive-verdicts.py when this review ends
fault_sites_why: the min()/max() accumulator keeps the SQLITE_STATIC zRoot pointer and compares against it after jsonEachCursorReset freed it; the comparison is binCollFunc, whose byte compare is memcmp, and the runners resolve only the faulting pc's symbol. Declared 2026-10-10 after the virtual runs resolved faults there, which is weaker than a pre-declaration. STRENGTHENED 2026-10-16: probe site 52 prints the pointer at the hand-out, at the free and at every comparison, so the catch no longer rests on 'any memcmp under this case'. On native memsys5, on virtual Capstone with lookaside off and on CheriBSD purecap alike, exactly three comparisons have as their FIRST operand the pointer that jsonEachCursorReset had already freed. The claim the verdict now rests on is that identity, not the function name
note: Re-measured 2026-10-16; every verdict holds, the mechanism is verified line by line in the pin, and the attribution is strengthened. Probe site 52 marks the SQLITE_STATIC hand-out in jsonEachColumn's default arm, the free in jsonEachCursorReset and the comparison in binCollFunc, judging both operands. The trace is the same on all three platforms: the hand-out of p=X, comparisons of X against itself while it is live, RESET frees X, the next cursor hands out a different buffer Y, and then three comparisons of the dead X against the live Y -- 24 probe events and 3 stale comparisons on virtual Capstone and on CheriBSD, the same 3 natively. witnesses=0 everywhere because memsys5 reissues the freed block, the blind spot case 05 documented, so the pointer identity is the evidence. Two record corrections: fidelity's cross-reference to 'case 18 (withdrawn, campaign numbering)' meant case 14, and fault_sites_why no longer claims only the function name. One limitation stated rather than resolved: the 'unfixed' label cannot be checked offline
